title: Probability of Combined Events
seo_title: Probability – JSS 3 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find the probability of combined events using sample spaces, tree diagrams, Venn diagrams and two-way tables. (summary of the NERDC JSS 3 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free JSS 3 maths worksheets on probability: two dice, coins and spinners, listing outcomes, Venn diagrams and two-way tables. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B) for independent events.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • For two events, list all the outcomes in a table (sample space). Two dice give 36 outcomes.
  • For independent events, P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B).
  • In a Venn diagram or two-way table, count the outcomes in the region you need and divide by the total.

Examples

Example

Two coins: P(two heads)

HH, HT, TH, TT

Answer: 1/4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting 11 outcomes for two diceThere are 6 × 6 = 36.
Adding when you should multiplyAnd means multiply for independent events.
Using the wrong totalCheck the total in the table.
